card.name: Sentence-ending punctuation in general web prose
card.fires_on: The period, exclamation mark or closing quote that ends a sentence in essays, news or blog text. It is strongest at the end of a paragraph or point, just before a new heading or a new topic starts.

modes.label: Period closing a point
modes.description: A full stop ends a rhetorical or opinion sentence, and the next sentence begins a new section or heading.
modes.example: When it does return, action on your part now will make it easier for you to deal with it then<<. >>How Inflation Affects Your Restaurant

modes.label: Exclamation or closing quote
modes.description: An exclamation mark or quote mark ends a sentence in promotional or quoted text.
modes.example: You could be a part of that future<<! >>The WHS Math and Science Academy will

modes.label: Space after a heading line
modes.description: A gap after a short title-like line, just before the body text begins.
